nvitk.gui.core.geometry¶

Screen-aware sizing for windows and dialogs.

Description¶

Every window in this GUI asks for the size it would like — resize(1700, 1000) for the Statmodels explorer, a setMinimumSize floor for each exploration dialog. On the machine those numbers were chosen on they are reasonable; on a 1366×768 laptop, an external monitor that was unplugged, or a scaled HiDPI display they are larger than the screen, and the result is a window whose controls sit past the edge with no way to reach them. A minimum size makes it worse than a plain oversize: the window cannot be shrunk back.

So preferences are expressed here as preferences. fit_to_screen() gives a widget the size it asked for or the largest that fits, whichever is smaller, and cap_minimum_size() keeps a floor from exceeding the screen.

Everything degrades to a no-op when no screen can be queried (offscreen tests, a headless CI run), because a layout hint is never worth failing a window over.

Module Contents¶

nvitk.gui.core.geometry.SCREEN_FRACTION: float = 0.92¶
nvitk.gui.core.geometry.MIN_WINDOW: tuple[int, int] = (640, 480)¶
nvitk.gui.core.geometry.available_screen_size(widget: Any = None) → tuple[int, int] | None¶

Usable (width, height) of the screen widget is on, excluding taskbars and docks.

Prefers the widget’s own screen so a window dragged to a second monitor is measured against that one. None when Qt cannot report a screen at all.

nvitk.gui.core.geometry.fit_to_screen(widget: Any, width: int, height: int) → tuple[int, int]¶

Resize widget to its preferred size, or to the largest that fits on screen.

Returns the size actually applied, so a caller can log or lay out against it.

Examples

A 1700×1000 request on a 1920×1080 desktop is honoured; on a 1366×768 laptop it becomes roughly 1256×706, and the window is fully reachable instead of running off two edges.

nvitk.gui.core.geometry.cap_minimum_size(widget: Any, width: int, height: int) → tuple[int, int]¶

Set a minimum size that the screen can actually accommodate.

A floor larger than the display is the one sizing mistake with no user-side recovery: the window cannot be shrunk, so whatever falls outside stays unreachable. This clamps the floor and leaves the widget resizable.

nvitk.gui.core.geometry.fit_dialog(widget: Any, width: int, height: int, *, minimum: tuple[int, int] = (520, 400)) → None¶

Size an exploration dialog: a modest hard floor, a preferred size, both clamped to the screen.

The floor is deliberately far below the preferred size. A dialog’s “minimum” is usually the author’s idea of the smallest comfortable size, not the smallest workable one, and encoding comfort as a hard limit is what puts a window off a small screen.
